<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| principles | Keep acts thin and services port-injected. Ownership path comparisons return data, never permission failures. Reuse builderOwnsPath and logical POSIX paths; use one typed warning format, persist observations in receipts, and preserve actual check results separately. No amendment code. First increment keeps the coupled composition writer/reader/schema change together; subsequent startup and delivery changes reuse that warning seam. |
| composition_root | harness/cli/src/acts/builder.ts registers commands and renders existing envelopes; services/builder/composition-service.ts owns import and verify side effects. |
| contracts | Increment 1: CompositionReceipt.warnings is an optional array for historical read compatibility; new receipts write an array. Each OwnershipWarning contains exact file, owning_unit (one unit ID, or unmapped), and stage (import or verify). Multiple mapped owners yield separate rows. Scalar owner labels remain visible in the standard DD renderer; this is observation, never authorization., Import warnings describe pre-import PM integration; verify preserves import-stage warnings and replaces verify-stage warnings for the current candidate so retries do not accumulate stale current-state warnings. Owning units derive from the complete guide map, using existing prefix matching., The path comparison still propagates actual Git/ancestry failures with cause and fix. Crossing a mapped ownership path is always a successful comparison result. Real build/test failures remain red and persist warnings beside failure evidence., Reviewers read composition warnings alongside the artifact. No warning-resolution decision, declared_by field, policy flag, receipt mutation gate or additional review prerequisite is added., Later increments: reuse the same comparison for on-track and delivery; replace acknowledgement-dependent release with one optional self-check. Final CLI grammar will be fixed before those changes; do not ship speculative commands in increment 1., harness builder self-check &lt;packet&gt; --sha256 &lt;expected-packet-digest&gt;; no builder ack alias, selfCheckBuilderPacket(deps: BuilderDeps, input: SelfCheckInput): Promise&lt;BuilderResult&lt;SelfCheckReport&gt;&gt; in self-check-service.ts; all inspection mismatches become a successful report with BuilderIssue[] warnings, not refusal., {packet, expected:{packet_sha256,root?,source_sha?}, observed:{packet_sha256?,root?,source_sha?}, warnings:BuilderIssue[]}; no write or native transport operation. Each warning names cause and corrective next_action., Packet.source_sha optional for reading historical packets, populated on every new packet. nonce remains a correlation value only. canary optional for reading history, never produced or demanded by current flow., New DispatchReceipt.delivery optional transport outcome with message_id/outcome/recorded_at. Persist native observation before send, then CAS the observed work-packet delivery. It is a transport fact, not acknowledgement/permission. Retired acknowledgement/release remain historical decode fields only., Read explicitly selected bounded regular packet, measure digest even if mismatched, compare actual repository root and HEAD with packet workspace and source_sha. For a historical packet lacking source_sha, use its in-root digest-bound baseline. Missing/unreadable/invalid packet/baseline or Git inspection yields warnings and no pretend success observation. Do not read arbitrary baseline paths outside the checkout. No clock window, root challenge, cleanliness/metadata veto, native seat handshake or state write., Bind exact current packet, dispatch and external allocation digests to delivery peer/workspace/source/unit. Validate root/branch and baseline ancestry before mutation. Compare packet.source_sha when present. Do not consult AckReceipt, acknowledgement, release outcome, delivery outcome, nonce/time-window or canary. Existing coder path-ownership warning conversion is checkpoint 3, not this change., FsPort.readBytesNoFollow(path, {maxBytes, root?}) optionally uses the existing bounded opened-file/confinement reader for exact packet-byte hashing. One-argument callers keep their existing behavior. Baseline reads supply the actual repository root; invalid UTF-8 remains observed bytes plus a warning, not a decoded-text digest claim., Format evolution: current packets use builder/work-packet with source_sha; provisioning stages the missing package before native launch. Existing builder/packet schemas and historical packet/ack records remain unchanged/readable. This is an explicit new record schema, not a handshake shim or schema-validation bypass., harness builder on-track &lt;plan&gt; [--unit &lt;id&gt;] [--from &lt;ref&gt;] [--to &lt;ref&gt;] [--untracked], No mutation/readiness/review/seal prerequisite. With --unit compare that named unit map (mode unit), otherwise all PM maps. Default from is imported integration_sha for PM, otherwise sealed source_sha if available, otherwise HEAD with explicit basis=head; malformed existing basis is an issue, not silent fallback. Default to is HEAD plus tracked staged/unstaged work; --untracked explicitly adds new/untracked paths. Explicit --to compares committed range only. Resolve Git refs with --verify --end-of-options and report measured full SHAs. Invalid/unavailable inspection returns compared:false plus actionable issues, exit0. Never call builderHead because inspection works on main too., OnTrackReport {compared, mode:unit\|pm, unit_id?, basis?:explicit\|import\|baseline\|head, from?,to?,includes_worktree,includes_untracked,warnings:OwnershipWarning[],issues:BuilderIssue[]}. Warnings use delivery stage for named-unit comparisons and verify for PM, so automatic and self-serve comparison rows match; issues explain incomplete inspection. No mandatory receipt/write., ownership-service.ts now owns moved builderOwnsPath (no re-export), ownershipWarnings(units,paths,allowedUnits,stage,unitId?), and committedDeliveryPaths(readGit,from,to) -&gt; {commits,paths}. The latter reads every touched path including reverted changes; caller owns root/ancestry and actual replay checks. No import cycle with composition-service., GuideCheckReport/ReadinessReport/BaselineReceipt/DispatchReceipt/AdvanceResult may carry warnings. Guide ownership-only issues become warnings, never valid:false. Baseline and dispatch retain them; composition retains guide/delivery/import warnings and refreshes verify warnings; advance returns warning evidence rather than silently discarding it., Keep wrong actual checkout/branch/commit, forged/mismatched receipt bindings, duplicate native peer and rewritten baseline failures before mutation; each names cause+fix. Do not treat all E477 as ownership or discard real Git/structural/check errors. Git replay limitations are operational, not scope policing; do not invent unsafe merge replay. |
